claim: As of October 2026, Claude Code applies managed settings above user, project and local settings. An organization can deliver them from the claude.ai admin console (server-managed settings), through MDM or OS policy (macOS configuration profile, Windows registry), or as a managed-settings.json file at /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/ (macOS), /etc/claude-code/ (Linux and WSL) or C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\ (Windows). A managed-settings.d/ directory lets several teams own parts of one file-based policy. Settings layers from highest to lowest are managed policy, the --settings flag, .claude/settings.local.json, the shared project file .claude/settings.json, then the user file ~/.claude/settings.json.

notes: Drop-in directory: managed-settings.json is merged first, then every *.json in managed-settings.d/ in alphabetical order (numeric prefixes such as 10-telemetry.json, 20-security.json control order).

MDM or OS policy is checked for changes every 30 minutes and a managed settings file is reloaded when it changes. /status (the Setting sources line) and claude doctor show which policy applied.

claim: As of October 2026, managed settings can lock down permissions and extensions: allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly and permissions.disableBypassPermissionsMode make managed settings the only source of permission rules and disable --dangerously-skip-permissions; allowManagedHooksOnly restricts which hooks run; strictPluginOnlyCustomization limits skills, agents, hooks and MCP servers to plugins or managed settings; sandbox.enabled and sandbox.network.allowedDomains add OS-level isolation. Array settings such as permissions.allow and permissions.deny merge across sources, so developers can extend managed lists but not remove from them.

sources.title: Configure server-managed settings
sources.excerpt: "deny": ["Bash(curl *)", "Read(./.env)", "Read(./.env.*)", "Read(./secrets/**)"], "disableBypassPermissionsMode": "disable" ... "allowManagedPermissionRulesOnly": true

notes: The example deny rules Read(./.env) and Read(./secrets/**) are the documentation's own example policy. Permission rules and sandboxing cover different layers: denying WebFetch blocks the fetch tool, but with Bash allowed, curl can still reach any URL unless the sandbox network allowlist is on.

claim: As of October 2026, by default anyone running Claude Code can connect any MCP server they choose; Anthropic reviews connectors for its directory but does not security-audit or manage any MCP server. Administrators can deploy a fixed set with managed-mcp.json, provide remote servers to every user with managedMcpServers, or filter with allowedMcpServers, deniedMcpServers and allowManagedMcpServersOnly. managed-mcp.json cannot be delivered through server-managed settings, and credentials should not go in its env blocks because any user on the machine can read the file. Claude Code has no built-in registry that users can browse, so an approved list is shared on an internal page or distributed as plugins; claude mcp list shows which servers load.

claim: As of October 2026, MCP allowlist and denylist entries match servers by serverUrl (exact or with * wildcards), serverCommand (the exact command and arguments of a stdio server) or serverName. A serverName entry is not a security control because it is only the label a user assigns. A denylist match overrides everything. An unset allowedMcpServers allows all servers while an empty array allows none. With allowManagedMcpServersOnly set to true, user, project and local allowlists are ignored while denylists still merge from every scope. A blocked claude mcp add reports that the server is not allowed by enterprise policy.

claim: As of October 2026, Anthropic's glossary defines agentic coding as a workflow where the AI can read files, run commands and make changes autonomously while you watch, redirect or step away, as opposed to chat-based assistants that only respond with text you must apply yourself. Claude Code works in a loop of gathering context, taking action and verifying results. Plan mode (entered with Shift+Tab or /plan) lets Claude research and propose changes without editing source files. Non-interactive mode (claude -p, formerly called headless mode) runs a single prompt and exits, for CI and scripts. A hook is a user-defined handler that runs automatically at a fixed point in Claude Code's lifecycle, deterministically rather than at the model's discretion. A subagent is a specialized assistant with its own context window, tools and permissions that returns a summary. MCP is an open standard for connecting AI tools to external data sources and services.
